name: North Yorkshire
description: North Yorkshire is England's largest ceremonial county by area, stretching from the Yorkshire Dales and North York Moors to the North Sea coast. It combines spectacular rural landscapes with historic towns and cities such as York, Harrogate and Scarborough.

places.name: York
places.description: A walled cathedral city in North Yorkshire, home to the largest Gothic cathedral in Northern Europe, York Minster, and the best-preserved medieval streets in England, including the Shambles.

places.name: Harrogate
places.description: A genteel Victorian spa town in North Yorkshire, known for its Royal Pump Room, elegant gardens, and reputation as one of Britain's most pleasant places to live.

places.name: Craven
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire covering the market town of Skipton, known as the 'Gateway to the Dales.'

places.name: Hambleton
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire covering the Vale of York and part of the North York Moors, including the market town of Thirsk, associated with vet-turned-author James Herriot.

places.name: Richmondshire
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire named for the market town of Richmond and its Norman castle, gateway to the Yorkshire Dales.

places.name: Ryedale
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire covering the market town of Malton and the southern edge of the North York Moors, known for its food scene and Castle Howard nearby.

places.name: Middlesbrough
places.description: An industrial town on Teesside built rapidly in the 19th century around iron and steel production, once nicknamed 'Ironopolis.'

places.name: Scarborough
places.description: A traditional Yorkshire seaside resort, often credited as Britain's first seaside holiday town, with a medieval castle overlooking two sweeping bays.

places.name: Selby
places.description: A rural district in North Yorkshire around the market town of Selby, home to a magnificent Norman abbey and flat farmland toward the Vale of York.

places.name: Stockton-on-Tees
places.description: A town on Teesside straddling the River Tees, historically the starting point of the world's first passenger railway in 1825.

places.name: Redcar and Cleveland
places.description: A coastal borough historically part of Cleveland, combining the seaside resort of Redcar with the industrial legacy of Teesside's steelworks and a stretch of dramatic North Sea coastline.
